Privacy Policy

Effective date: 10 November 2026 — applies to the "Quran Meanings" (معاني القرآن) app on Android and iOS.

Your privacy matters. The app needs no account, shows no ads, and does not collect your name, email address, or phone number. This page explains plainly the little data that is collected, why, where it goes, and how you can control it.

In short

  • No accounts and no sign-in; we collect no identifying data about you.
  • No ads, no ad networks, and we do not collect the device advertising ID.
  • We never sell your data or share it for marketing.
  • We use Google's Firebase for usage statistics and crash reports, solely to improve the app and fix its bugs.
  • Your approximate location is used only to fetch prayer times, and only if you choose that yourself.
  • The app's content (the Quran, tafsir, word meanings, and azkar) is bundled inside the app and works offline.

Usage statistics (Firebase Analytics)

To understand how the app is used and which parts need improvement, the app sends the following to Google's Firebase Analytics service:

  • Which screens are opened and general in-app events (for example, opening the surah list or the Settings screen). Ayah text, search queries, and bookmark contents are never sent.
  • Device model, operating-system version, and app version.
  • Country-level region, which Google's servers infer from the IP address at the time of sending.
  • The Firebase installation ID: a random identifier for this installation only. It is not linked to your name or any account and changes when you reinstall the app.

Crash reports (Firebase Crashlytics)

If the app crashes or hits an unexpected error, Crashlytics sends a report containing the crash log and stack trace, the device state at the moment of the crash (model, OS version, available memory, screen orientation, and connectivity), the app version, and the Firebase installation ID. These reports are used only to diagnose and fix bugs.

Who receives this data and how long it is kept

Analytics and crash data are sent to Google LLC through the Firebase service, which processes them on our behalf as a data processor under the Firebase privacy and security terms and the Google Privacy Policy. Data is encrypted in transit.

  • The app does not collect the Android Advertising ID or the iOS IDFA, and none of the above is used for advertising or to track you across other apps and websites.
  • Retention: analytics and crash data are kept for Firebase's default retention periods, and we keep no copies outside Firebase.

Location (prayer times)

The whole app works without your location. On the Prayer Times screen you can pick a city from the list manually, or tap "Use my location". The app asks for the location permission only when you tap that button. Once it is granted, the app may read your location again while it is open (never in the background) if no city has been saved yet. When your location is used:

  • The app asks for the approximate (city-level) location permission. On Android versions older than Android 12 the system may rely on GPS to supply the location, but the purpose and use do not change.
  • Your coordinates are sent to the AlAdhan service (api.aladhan.com) to fetch prayer times for your area; that service's own privacy policy applies to it.
  • We do not store your coordinates on any server of ours. The resulting prayer times and the last location used are saved locally on your device so the screen works offline.
  • You can revoke the location permission at any time in your device settings; the rest of the app keeps working as usual.

Mushaf page fonts

When you choose the "Mushaf pages" reading mode, the app downloads the page fonts (King Fahd Complex QCF V4 fonts, one per page) on demand from the content delivery network of Tarteel's Quranic Universal Library (QUL) at static-cdn.tarteel.ai. As with any download over the internet, that server sees your device's IP address and the requested page number; the app sends no identifier or other data. The fonts are stored on your device after download.

Web search

On the word-search screen, the "Search the web" button opens your device's browser on Google search results for the word you typed. At that point you have left the app for Google's website, and Google's privacy policy applies. The app itself does not send your query to any server.

Data stored on your device

Your preferences are saved locally on your device: language, theme, text size, reading position, bookmarks, notification settings, a cached copy of prayer times, and any mushaf fonts you downloaded. All of it is deleted when you uninstall the app.

  • On Android, your preferences are included in Android Auto Backup to your own Google account, encrypted, and we have no access to them.
  • On iOS, the app's data is included in your device backup (iCloud or computer).
  • You can turn off backup for the app in your operating-system settings.

Children

The app is suitable for all ages. We do not knowingly collect any personal data from children; what is collected from any user is limited to what is described above, and none of it is identifying.

Your choices

  • To stop usage statistics and crash reports: uninstall the app. There is currently no in-app switch to turn them off.
  • To stop location use: revoke the location permission in your device settings, or pick a city manually.
  • To stop backup: disable it for the app in Android or iCloud settings.
  • To request deletion of the data associated with your installation in Firebase: email us at the address below.

Changes to this policy

If anything material changes, we will publish the updated version on this page and update the effective date.
